name: TX-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by eleven points, anchoring the race to the incumbent's side
Keith Self is a sitting incumbent with a clear cash advantage and outside backing
Challenger Evan Hunt has spent down to about $44,000 on hand with no outside support
Prediction markets price a Republican hold at roughly 94 percent
model.rationale: An eleven-point Republican district plus an incumbent holding a large cash edge leaves Hunt needing an unusually favorable national environment to compete; with no polls or expert ratings available, the funding gap and market pricing near 94 percent for the Republican point to a margin beyond a mere district-lean estimate.
model.watch: A sharp national swing against Republicans in 2026, or Hunt suddenly out-raising Self and drawing major outside spending, would be the clearest signals this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 3rd District, anchored in Collin County north of Dallas, leans Republican by about eleven points, and incumbent Keith Self is seeking another term. Self holds a clear financial edge, with roughly $213,000 on hand to Evan Hunt's $44,000, and has drawn modest outside support while Hunt has drawn none. Hunt has raised a respectable sum overall but spent most of it, leaving limited resources for the general election.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, and prediction markets give Republicans about a 94 percent chance of holding the seat. The structural factors in the contest — district lean, incumbency, and money — all point in the same direction. Hunt would need a substantially worse national environment for Republicans than current fundamentals suggest to put this seat genuinely in play.
